title: Leakage and Contamination Audit
baseline_record_text: EXP-CTRL-A03 — Leakage and Contamination Audit Priority: A Evidence State: R Associated Claims: CORE-001, SFR-A001, COSMO-L001 Objective Determine whether historical S.T.A.R. machine-learning and feature-engineering experiments contain information leakage between training and testing populations. Historical motivation Several historical scripts construct: ● normalized variables; ● redshift bins; ● (L_{\rm cosmo}(s)); ● cosmo_rank; ● interaction terms; before the train/test split. Therefore historical performance values cannot automatically be interpreted as leakage-free predictive measurements. Procedure Reconstruct the relevant pipelines so that: [ D_{\rm train} \rightarrow \text{fit preprocessing} \rightarrow D_{\rm train}^{\prime}, ] and the fitted transformations are subsequently applied to: [ D_{\rm test} \rightarrow D_{\rm test}^{\prime}. ] No target-derived or population-derived quantity may be calculated using the complete dataset before partitioning. Required controls Compare: 1. historical pipeline; 2. leakage-controlled pipeline; 3. shuffled-target pipeline. Success Criterion The reconstructed pipeline must reproduce the historical result within a documented tolerance where no leakage is present. Failure Criterion Any material performance degradation attributable to information leakage must be recorded and the historical result reclassified accordingly.

title: Random-Feature Baseline
baseline_record_text: EXP-CTRL-A01 — Random-Feature Baseline Priority: A Evidence State: C/R Associated Claim: CTRL-RF001 Objective Establish a non-theoretical machine-learning baseline. Historical basis model5.py used random feature selection and a fixed random seed for predictive modeling. Design Construct a baseline using randomly selected astrophysical features under a fixed seed. Compare against: ● ordinary astrophysical baseline; ● arithmetic-feature baseline; ● arithmetic-plus-astrophysical model. Primary endpoint Out-of-sample: [ R^2_{\rm OOS}. ] Secondary: [ {\rm RMSE},\quad {\rm MAE}. ] Purpose Determine whether an apparent improvement from S.T.A.R. features exceeds ordinary feature-selection effects.

title: Arithmetic Permutation Control
baseline_record_text: EXP-CTRL-A02 — Arithmetic Permutation Control Priority: A Evidence State: N Associated Claims: SFR-A001, ARITH-001 Objective Determine whether arithmetic-derived features contain information beyond their marginal distributions and accidental correlations. Procedure Preserve the marginal distribution of each arithmetic feature while breaking its association with the astronomical target. Possible permutation procedures include: \pi(X_{\rm arith}). ] Where appropriate, permutations should preserve relevant grouping variables. Comparison [ X_{\rm astro} ] versus [ X_{\rm astro}+X_{\rm arith} ] versus [ X_{\rm astro}+X_{\rm arith}^{\rm perm}. ] Primary endpoint [ \Delta R^2_{\rm OOS}. ] Success Criterion The unpermuted arithmetic model must outperform the appropriately constructed permutation distribution at a pre-registered significance level.

title: Log-Normal Reciprocal-Normalization Test
baseline_record_text: EXP-K001 — Log-Normal Reciprocal-Normalization Test Priority: A Evidence State: R Associated Claim: MATH-K001 Historical construction \sum_{i=1}^{N} \left(\frac{M_0}{M_i}\right)^s ] with normalization \frac{\sum_i(M_i/M_0)} {\sum_i(M_0/M_i)}. ] For a log-normal mass distribution with [ \log M_i\sim N(\mu,\sigma^2), ] and [ M_0=e^\mu, ] the historical derivation gives equal limiting expectations for the numerator and denominator, suggesting [ K_{\rm theory}\rightarrow1. ] Objective Separate this statistical result from its historical BSD-inspired interpretation. Experimental groups 1. Gaussian-log mass distribution; 2. skewed distribution; 3. heavy-tailed distribution; 4. mixture distribution; 5. empirical galaxy-mass distributions. Variables [ N,\quad \mu,\quad\sigma,\quad K. ] Primary analysis Estimate: [ E[K_N],\quad {\rm Var}(K_N) ] as a function of (N). Historical observations The R&D archive contains simulations with approximately: [ N=500,\qquad \mu=9.7843,\qquad \sigma=0.3645, ] and reported mean: [ K\approx0.998108. ] Historical observational samples also produced materially different values, including small-(N) results. These are treated as reconstruction targets, not established confirmations. Success Criterion The theoretical convergence behavior is reproduced under the stated assumptions and its finite-sample behavior is characterized.

Core construction \sum_i \left(\frac{M_0}{M_i}\right)^s. ] Historical implementations also introduced redshift binning and derived mass-dependent quantities. Critical requirement All population statistics and normalization parameters must be estimated within the training fold. Baselines 1. mass-only; 2. mass + redshift; 3. standard astrophysical feature set; 4. astrophysical + (L_{\rm cosmo}); 5. shuffled (L_{\rm cosmo}). Primary endpoint Incremental out-of-sample predictive information: [ \Delta R^2_{\rm OOS}. ] Secondary endpoints [ \Delta {\rm RMSE}, \quad \Delta {\rm MAE}, \quad \text{calibration error}. ] Success (L_{\rm cosmo}) demonstrates reproducible incremental information on independent data.

title: Arithmetic Incremental SFR Prediction
baseline_record_text: EXP-SFR-A01 — Arithmetic Incremental SFR Prediction Priority: A Evidence State: N/R Associated Claim: SFR-A001 Hypothesis Arithmetic-derived variables may provide information about SFR beyond ordinary astrophysical variables. Target [ Y=\log{\rm SFR}_{H\alpha}. ] Baseline [ Y=f(X_{\rm astro}). ] Extended model [ Y=f(X_{\rm astro},X_{\rm arith}). ] where (X_{\rm arith}) may include: [ r_E,\quad \log|\Delta_E|,\quad \log N_E,\quad \log\operatorname{Reg}(E),\quad T_E, ] and validated mapping-derived variables. Primary endpoint R^2_{\rm arithmetic+astro} R^2_{\rm astro}. ] Secondary endpoints ● RMSE; ● MAE; ● residual distributions; ● calibration; ● SHAP stability; ● performance across SFR strata. Critical control Arithmetic permutation control EXP-CTRL-A02. Success Criterion An incremental effect survives: ● leakage-controlled preprocessing; ● held-out testing; ● permutation control; ● multiple random seeds; ● independent dataset validation. A statistically significant effect without practical predictive value is not sufficient for Level 4 predictive correspondence.

title: Extreme-SFR Robustness
baseline_record_text: EXP-SFR-A03 — Extreme-SFR Robustness Priority: A Evidence State: R/N Associated Claim: SFR-E001 Historical motivation Historical models showed substantially different behavior for extreme-SFR populations compared with the bulk population. One historical analysis reported approximately: ● full-sample RF (R^2\approx0.8455); ● full-sample GB (R^2\approx0.8476); ● non-outlier RF (R^2\approx0.8729); ● non-outlier GB (R^2\approx0.8766); with substantially poorer performance in the extreme/outlier population. These historical values require reconstruction under controlled preprocessing. Design Pre-register SFR strata rather than defining outliers after observing model performance. Evaluate: [ R^2,\quad {\rm RMSE},\quad {\rm MAE} ] within each stratum. Objective Determine whether arithmetic features retain any incremental information specifically in extreme-SFR populations.

title: Rank and Cosmic Environment
baseline_record_text: EXP-RANK-A01 — Rank and Cosmic Environment Priority: A Evidence State: N Associated Claims: RANK-001, RANK-002 Hypothesis Elliptic-curve rank may exhibit statistically nontrivial correspondence with cosmic environment. Test variables Rank: [ r_E. ] Environmental variables may include: ● galaxy density; ● local density; ● cluster membership; ● filament membership; ● void membership; ● environmental classification. Primary analysis Estimate: [ P(r_E\mid{\rm environment}) ] and compare against appropriate null distributions. Nulls ● random assignment of elliptic curves to galaxies; ● permutation of rank labels; ● matched environmental sampling; ● alternative arithmetic invariants. Important distinction The experiment does not assume: [ r=0\Rightarrow{\rm void}, ] or any other one-to-one physical interpretation. Those are hypotheses to be tested.

title: Rank-Weighted Cosmic Topology
baseline_record_text: EXP-RANK-A02 — Rank-Weighted Cosmic Topology Priority: A Evidence State: N/R Associated Claims: RANK-003, TOPO-001, TOPO-002 Hypothesis Arithmetic rank may contribute information about cosmic-web topology. Construction Define a rank-weighted filtration: [ K_\epsilon^{(r)}. ] The exact construction must be fixed before the final comparison. Topological observables Persistent homology: [ \beta_0,\quad\beta_1,\quad\beta_2. ] Interpretation: ● (\beta_0): connected-component structure; ● (\beta_1): one-dimensional cycles/connectivity; ● (\beta_2): cavities/void structure. Persistent homology must not be interpreted as a direct filament counter. Filaments Filament identification should primarily use: ● geometric skeleton methods; ● graph methods; ● established cosmic-web classifiers. Persistent homology provides supporting topological information. Comparison [ D_{\rm arith} \leftrightarrow D_{\rm cosmic}. ] Use: ● Wasserstein distance; ● bottleneck distance; ● persistence landscapes/images; ● topology-aware statistics. Null models ● randomized rank assignments; ● randomized arithmetic mappings; ● spatial shuffling; ● density-preserving controls. Historical values such as: [ W_2<10^{-2} ] are exploratory/model-dependent and are not accepted as universal evidence thresholds.

title: Null-Calibrated Persistent Homology
baseline_record_text: EXP-TOPO-A01 — Null-Calibrated Persistent Homology Priority: A Evidence State: R/N Associated Claims: TOPO-001, TOPO-002, TOPO-003 Objective Establish whether any observed arithmetic/topological correspondence exceeds what can be produced by the null models. Required analysis For each mapping: [ D_{\rm observed} ] must be compared against an empirical null distribution: [ D_{\rm null}^{(1)},\ldots,D_{\rm null}^{(N)}. ] Output Report: ● effect size; ● empirical (p)-value; ● confidence interval; ● null distribution; ● multiple-comparison correction where applicable; ● sensitivity to resolution; ● sensitivity to sampling density; ● sensitivity to noise; ● mapping sensitivity. Success Criterion Observed correspondence must survive the pre-registered null ensemble.

title: Arithmetic Generator Controls
baseline_record_text: EXP-MAP-A03 — Arithmetic Generator Controls Priority: A Evidence State: N/R Historical construction Fibonacci and Lucas sequences have been used to construct arithmetic parameters. Objective Determine whether the observed correspondence depends on those specific sequences. Controls Compare: ● Fibonacci; ● Lucas; ● prime sequences; ● randomized recurrence sequences; ● matched-complexity alternative sequences. Requirement Sequence complexity and parameter count must be controlled as closely as possible. Interpretation A Fibonacci/Lucas result that is reproduced equally well by arbitrary matched-complexity sequences does not establish a special Fibonacci/Lucas correspondence.
